Real-world applications of how animals see, hear, smell

concepts.title: Animals That Are Active at Night
concepts.description: Animals That Are Active at Night — part of the chapter on Super Senses.
key_ideas: Core principles of animals that are active at night
Step-by-step problem solving for animals that are active at night
Real-world applications of animals that are active at night

concepts.title: Super Sense of Smell: Ants and Insects
concepts.description: Explores how insects like ants and silkworms use their powerful sense of smell to navigate, find food, and locate mates.
key_ideas: Ants leave a chemical trail (smell) on the ground to guide others.
Mosquitoes find humans by body smell and heat.
Silkworms can find female moths from kilometers away by smell.

concepts.title: Sensing Sounds and Vibrations
concepts.description: Differentiates between hearing through ears and sensing vibrations through the ground, focusing on snakes and tigers.
key_ideas: Snakes do not have external ears; they feel vibrations on the ground.
Tigers use whiskers to sense movements and vibrations in the air.
Sharp hearing helps predators catch prey and prey to escape.

concepts.title: Animal Languages and Warning Signals
concepts.description: Examines how animals use special sounds and behaviors to communicate danger to their groups.
key_ideas: Langurs and birds make special alarm calls to warn of dangers like tigers or leopards.
Different sounds are used for different dangers (e.g., danger from sky vs. ground).
Some animals behave differently before natural disasters like earthquakes.

concepts.title: Sleeping Patterns and Hibernation
concepts.description: Investigates the varied sleeping habits of animals, including duration of sleep and seasonal deep sleep.
key_ideas: Sloths sleep for nearly 17 hours a day while hanging upside down.
Some animals, like lizards, go into a long deep sleep (hibernation) during winter.
Comparison of sleep duration between cows, pythons, giraffes, and cats.

concepts.title: Poaching and Animal Protection
concepts.description: Discusses why animals are hunted for their special body parts and the importance of national parks.
key_ideas: Poaching is the illegal killing of animals for tusks, skin, horns, or musk.
The relationship between an animal's 'super sense' organ and why humans hunt them.
National Parks and Sanctuaries exist to protect animals and their habitats.

concepts.title: How Seeds Travel
concepts.description: How Seeds Travel — part of the chapter on Seeds and Seeds.
key_ideas: Core principles of how seeds travel
Step-by-step problem solving for how seeds travel
Real-world applications of how seeds travel

concepts.title: Germination — Seed to Plant
concepts.description: Germination — Seed to Plant — part of the chapter on Seeds and Seeds.
key_ideas: Core principles of germination
Step-by-step problem solving for germination
Real-world applications of germination

concepts.title: What is Inside a Seed?
concepts.description: Exploration of the internal structure of a seed, identifying the protective and nutritive parts necessary for a baby plant to survive.
key_ideas: The seed coat protects the seed
Cotyledons (seed leaves) store food
The embryo is the baby plant waiting to grow

concepts.title: Experiments with Sprouting
concepts.description: Analyzing the specific environmental conditions required for seeds to sprout effectively through observation and experimentation (e.g., wet cotton vs. submerged in water).
key_ideas: Seeds need air, water, and warmth to sprout
Seeds submerged completely in water cannot breathe
Dry seeds do not change or grow

concepts.title: Plants that Hunt
concepts.description: Introduction to carnivorous plants, specifically the Pitcher plant (Nepenthes), explaining how and why some plants trap insects.
key_ideas: Some plants eat insects to get nutrients
The Pitcher plant uses smell to attract insects
These plants are often found in areas with poor soil

concepts.title: Inventions from Nature: The Story of Velcro
concepts.description: Understanding how observing seed characteristics (like hooks and burrs) led to human inventions, specifically the creation of Velcro by George Mestral.
key_ideas: George Mestral observed seeds sticking to his dog
Nature can inspire human inventions (Biomimicry)
Velcro mimics the tiny hooks found on certain seeds

concepts.title: Who Came from Where? (Vegetable Origins)
concepts.description: Tracing the geographical origins of common vegetables to understand that humans also help seeds travel across continents over history.
key_ideas: Chillies came to India from South America
Cabbage and peas came from Europe
Humans carry seeds across oceans for trade and food

concepts.title: Things That Dissolve in Water
concepts.description: Things That Dissolve in Water — part of the chapter on Experiments with Water.
key_ideas: Core principles of things that dissolve in water
Step-by-step problem solving for things that dissolve in water
Real-world applications of things that dissolve in water

concepts.title: Evaporation and Condensation
concepts.description: Evaporation and Condensation — part of the chapter on Experiments with Water.
key_ideas: Core principles of evaporation and condensation
Step-by-step problem solving for evaporation and condensation
Real-world applications of evaporation and condensation

concepts.title: Floating and Sinking
concepts.description: Understanding why certain objects float on the surface of water while others sink to the bottom based on their material and shape.
key_ideas: Lighter objects usually float, heavy objects usually sink
Shape affects floating (e.g., an iron ship floats, but an iron nail sinks)
Displacement of water helps things float

concepts.title: Mixing Oil and Water
concepts.description: Observing the behavior of oil when mixed with water and understanding why they do not mix (immiscibility).
key_ideas: Oil does not dissolve in water
Oil forms a separate layer on top of water
Liquids that do not mix are called immiscible

concepts.title: Factors Affecting Dissolving Speed
concepts.description: Investigating how different conditions change how quickly a substance dissolves in water.
key_ideas: Stirring water makes things dissolve faster
Heating water increases the speed of dissolving
Powdered substances dissolve faster than solid lumps

concepts.title: The Magic of Salt Water (Density)
concepts.description: Exploring how adding salt to water changes its properties, allowing objects that normally sink (like a lemon or egg) to float.
key_ideas: Salt water is 'thicker' (denser) than fresh water
Objects float easier in salty water
The Dead Sea is so salty that people can float without swimming

concepts.title: Symbols on Maps
concepts.description: Symbols on Maps — part of the chapter on Mapping Our Neighbourhood.
key_ideas: Core principles of symbols on maps
Step-by-step problem solving for symbols on maps
Real-world applications of symbols on maps

concepts.title: Scale and Distance
concepts.description: Scale and Distance — part of the chapter on Mapping Our Neighbourhood.
key_ideas: Core principles of scale and distance
Step-by-step problem solving for scale and distance
Real-world applications of scale and distance

concepts.title: Aerial Perspective (Top View)
concepts.description: Understanding that maps are drawn from a 'bird's eye view' or top-down perspective, looking different than objects seen from the side.
key_ideas: Definition of aerial view
How 3D objects look in 2D from above
Difference between a photograph and a map

concepts.title: Cardinal Directions
concepts.description: Learning the four main directions (North, South, East, West) to orient a map correctly.
key_ideas: Identifying North, South, East, and West
Using a Compass Rose
Orienting a map relative to the real world

concepts.title: Navigating Routes
concepts.description: Using directions and landmarks to trace a path from one location to another on a map.
key_ideas: Tracing paths between two points
Identifying left and right turns relative to the path
Describing a route using landmarks

concepts.title: Zooming In and Out
concepts.description: Comparing maps of different sizes, such as a map of a classroom versus a map of a city or country, to understand detail and coverage.
key_ideas: Relationship between area covered and detail shown
Hierarchy: Room -> School -> City -> State
Why different maps are used for different purposes

concepts.title: Who Does What — Division of Labour
concepts.description: Who Does What — Division of Labour — part of the chapter on Social Topics.
key_ideas: Core principles of who does what
Step-by-step problem solving for who does what
Real-world applications of who does what

concepts.title: Similarities and Differences Among People
concepts.description: Similarities and Differences Among People — part of the chapter on Social Topics.
key_ideas: Core principles of similarities and differences among people
Step-by-step problem solving for similarities and differences among people
Real-world applications of similarities and differences among people

concepts.title: Gender Roles and Breaking Stereotypes
concepts.description: Explores societal expectations for boys and girls, challenging the idea that certain tasks or sports are meant only for one gender.
key_ideas: Understanding gender stereotypes in household work and sports
Equal opportunities for girls and boys
Overcoming social barriers to pursue dreams (e.g., girls in sports)

concepts.title: Dignity of Labour and Social Justice
concepts.description: Discusses the respectability of all types of work, specifically addressing sanitation work, untouchability, and the teachings of Mahatma Gandhi regarding social equality.
key_ideas: No work is 'small' or 'dirty'
The importance of sanitation workers in society
Gandhiji's efforts to remove untouchability and promote equality

concepts.title: Team Spirit and Cooperation
concepts.description: Focuses on the importance of working together towards a common goal, particularly through the lens of team sports and group activities.
key_ideas: Playing for the team rather than for oneself
Cooperation and mutual respect among team members
Resolving conflicts constructively within a group

concepts.title: Migration, Displacement, and Changing Lives
concepts.description: Examines why families move from villages to cities or other areas, covering voluntary migration for work and forced displacement due to development projects like dams.
key_ideas: Differences between village life and city life
Challenges faced by migrant families (schooling, housing, language)
Impact of displacement due to construction of dams and factories

concepts.title: Public Property and Community Responsibility
concepts.description: Identifies shared resources within a community and the collective responsibility to maintain and protect them.
key_ideas: Difference between private and public property
Caring for parks, schools, buses, and historical monuments
Role of citizens in maintaining community hygiene and order
